opening.eyebrow: ClickUp · Delivery Command · Proof of concept
opening.subtitle: One Monday in ClickUp delivery: portfolio, project, staffing, scope change, customer sign-off, weekly summary and an AI status report, all on one record.

closing.title: Plan, staff and report *every rollout in one place*.
closing.subtitle: Delivery Command, built on UnifyApps for ClickUp's delivery team.
closing.cta: Next: agree the pilot scope with ClickUp delivery

acts.title: See the risk
acts.goal: The delivery director spots Halden Freight at risk and opens it.

scenes.title: Portfolio
scenes.mode: live (Storage reads); the risk card is seeded and marked AI-written
scenes.narration: Monday morning. Ines Moreau, the delivery director, opens Portfolio: 14 on track, 4 at risk, up one, and 2 off track, up one, since last week. A risk card, marked AI-written, flags Halden Freight with high confidence and shows its evidence. On the risk grid, the migration risk sits at likelihood 4 and impact 4, and the trend has fallen to 70 percent on track. She filters to Europe and At risk: 2 of 20 projects. A note says the Jira sync has failed since 06:40.

actions.say: Point out the On track, At risk and Off track tiles
Point out the AI-written risk card for Halden Freight
Point out RSK-1183 in the likelihood 4 by impact 4 cell
Add the Region Europe and Health At risk chips to the project table
Point out the Jira sync failed note

scenes.title: Project overview
scenes.narration: She opens Halden Freight. The seven-stage path stands at Migration, with go-live on November 27, 512 of 640 budget hours used, 5 open RAID items, and Migration plan v2 due on October 28. The Migration column holds 16 tasks against a 15 task limit, and says so. Mira Castell, the lead, moves Validate pilot batch on to Training from the card's menu, the keyboard path. The move is recorded, and the task detail opens beside the board.

actions.say: Click Open project on the risk card
Point out the Migration column's over-limit warning
Open the Validate pilot batch card menu and choose Move to stage, Training
The task detail opens beside the board

acts.title: Staff and change
acts.card: Staff the work, *change the plan with approval*.
acts.goal: A booking that would overload a consultant is refused; a scope change routes to the right approvers.

scenes.title: The refusal: over capacity
scenes.narration: As resource manager, she books Tomas Brandt onto Halden Freight for 8 hours a week in the weeks of November 2 and November 9, from a form, with no dragging. The app refuses before anything is saved. Over capacity: Tomas would be at 120 percent in the week of November 2, eight hours over, and 105 percent in the week of November 9, two hours over. She filters the skills matrix to data migration, finds Lena Vogt, and books her instead.

actions.say: Choose Tomas Brandt, Halden Freight, weeks Nov 2 and Nov 9, 8 hours, then Book
Point out the Over capacity refusal naming who, which weeks and by how much
Open Skills, filter to Data migration, then book Lena Vogt

scenes.title: Change request
scenes.mode: live (ClickUp DC · Submit change request, ClickUp DC · Decide change request)
scenes.narration: To protect the date, Mira raises a change request: a third migration batch, 48 extra hours, 7,200 euros of cost, and 7 days to the go-live. Before submitting, she sees the plan before and after, side by side, with the differences marked. At 40 hours or more, it routes to Ines Moreau, the delivery director, then Raj Patel, the finance partner. Both approve, and Halden Freight's go-live moves to December 4.

actions.say: Fill reason, work added, 48 hours, EUR 7,200, go-live +7 days
Point out the before and after plans with the differences marked
Submit; the approval path names the director, then the finance partner
Approve as the director, then as the finance partner

acts.title: The customer signs off
acts.card: The customer signs off, *in their own language*.
acts.goal: The sponsor sees only her project, in German, and signs off.

scenes.title: Customer portal
scenes.narration: Now the customer's side. Katrin Albers, Halden Freight's sponsor, opens the portal in German. She sees only her own project: stage, milestones, sessions, open actions and shared documents, with no internal health score, and dates written the German way, like 28.10.2026. Under Freigaben, she signs off Migration plan v2. The sign-off records who approved and when, and lands in the project's activity feed.

actions.say: Switch the portal to Deutsch
Point out the German date format
Open Freigaben and click Freigeben on Migration plan v2

acts.title: Lead and report
acts.card: Read the week, *draft the report with AI*.
acts.goal: The VP reads the Monday summary; the lead drafts and publishes a status report with Delivery Copilot.

scenes.title: Weekly summary
scenes.mode: seeded (snapshot rows, not presented as AI); the email is mocked as a preview
scenes.narration: Every Monday, the VP of customer success reads one page. Six headline numbers show their change from last week, coloured by whether it is good or bad for the business: 6 projects at risk, 2 more than last week, shown as bad. The contract value bridge runs from 4.05 million at the start to 4.21 million at the end, in US dollars. Below sit the 5 projects that changed most, each with its reason, and a sample of the 08:00 Monday email for each region, shown here, not sent. In this demo, the summary is a seeded weekly snapshot.

actions.say: Point out Projects at risk, 6, +2 shown as bad
Point out the contract value bridge
Scroll to the five projects and the Monday email sample

scenes.title: Delivery Copilot and the status report
scenes.mode: live (the agent and ClickUp DC · Publish status report)
scenes.narration: Back on Halden Freight, Mira opens Delivery Copilot, a read-only AI agent, with 3 suggested questions. She asks which Europe projects go live in November and are at risk. The panel shows the step it is working on, then answers Halden Freight, with a link to the project. Then she asks for this week's status report. The AI-written draft cites the late migration tasks, the migration risk, and 512 of 640 budget hours. She brings it into the report, edits one line and publishes, well inside the 10 minute target.

target.text: Which Europe projects go live in November and are at risk?

actions.say: Click the suggested question: Which Europe projects go live in November and are at risk?

target.text: Draft this week's status report for Halden Freight

actions.say: Click: Draft this week's status report for Halden Freight
Put the draft in the report editor, edit one line, click Publish
actions.at: She brings it into the report

acts.title: Under the hood
acts.card: Under the hood: *rules and an agent you can read*.
acts.goal: The capacity rule on the automation canvas, and the Copilot's set-up in the agent builder.

scenes.title: Book consultant on the canvas
scenes.narration: Under the hood, the refusal came from one automation, Book consultant. On its canvas, it reads the consultant, the project and every booking, adds the new hours week by week against weekly capacity, and refuses any week over 100 percent without writing anything.

actions.say: Open ClickUp DC · Book consultant on the automation canvas; point out its steps

scenes.title: Delivery Copilot in the agent builder
scenes.narration: The Copilot is set up in the agent builder: plain instructions, one tool that reads delivery data, and a chart tool. It has no tool that writes, so it drafts and explains, and people decide and publish.

actions.say: Open ClickUp Delivery Copilot in the agent builder; point out instructions and tools
